title: Dot

seo.title: Dot Lifestyle Hero Section Design & Prompt | Ottermind
seo.description: Hero section reference for a lifestyle brand — #0871E7 accent, a dark stage, React and Tailwind CSS and 100ms transitions. Copy the prompt or open it staged in Studio.

tagline: Hero section reference built on white #DEF0FC and bright blue #0871E7, set in Instrument Serif and measured against type from 14px to 72px.
summary: Hero section reference for a lifestyle brand — #0871E7 accent, a dark stage, React and Tailwind CSS and 100ms transitions.
about: Dot solves the hero section problem for a lifestyle brand with a single captured brief. The palette runs white #DEF0FC underneath, black #1A1A1A for the type and bright blue #0871E7 carrying the accents, and the type is Instrument Serif. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 800x588 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The brief spends its motion budget on 100ms transitions. Use it as the reference when you are building a lifestyle brand hero section and want a finished composition instead of a starting point.

layout.title: A bar with nothing spare
layout.body: The bar carries the wordmark, the section links and one #0871E7 button, measured at type from 14px to 72px and 14px spacing steps so it never grows into a second header. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #0871E7 action is the only element in the bar with any weight. If your own page has more sections, group them rather than widening the bar.

layout.title: Copy first, decoration second
layout.body: The whole composition fits one screen and is delivered as React and Tailwind CSS, with the copy, the media and the controls named in the brief. The page is one composition at 800x588, which is why it holds together when the copy changes.

layout.title: Navigation held to one row
layout.body: The bar sits over the 800x588 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Nothing here is inherited
layout.body: Every measurement in the brief is a number you can measure back: type from 14px to 72px, 14px spacing steps and 100ms transitions. There is no invented intermediate value between the named ones; the measurement list is the whole system.

motion.title: Durations from the brief
motion.body: The animation budget is small and explicit: 100ms, applied to state changes rather than to entrances. One value is reused across the controls, so their timing cannot drift apart.

motion.title: Hover where it means something
motion.body: Feedback is limited to hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, so the rest of the layout is a fixed composition. The interactive states do not move layout, so nothing jumps under the pointer. Do not animate layout on hover.

notes: The type is set in Instrument Serif on a 14–72px scale, and the spacing follows the same steps.
The accent is spent on bright blue #0871E7 and the rest of the composition holds white #DEF0FC.
The display line is Instrument Serif at the top of a 14–72px scale, with the interface text on the same face.

customize: Retune #0871E7 for your brand only after the Instrument Serif copy is final, and re-check the contrast on the darkest band.
Keep the supporting line as short as the reference's and measure the pair against the 800x588 crop.
Change #0871E7 for your brand accent and re-check it against #DEF0FC, because the accent is the only saturated value in this composition.
The brief behind this page is written out in full below, so any rewrite can be checked against it value by value; the reference was captured at 800x588.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the hero section
editorial.body: The page has more numbers in it than it appears to. type from 14px to 72px, 14px spacing steps and 100ms transitions are the ones a rebuild has to keep; the rest can move. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

editorial.title: What holds up for Lifestyle
editorial.body: Dot is the hero section reference for a lifestyle brand, and it answers the problem that audience actually has. The palette stays disciplined (white #DEF0FC and bright blue #0871E7) and the type is set in Instrument Serif, so nothing in the composition depends on a borrowed trend. When you brief a build, this is the part worth copying: one promise at display size, with the supporting detail held below it. It gives a lifestyle reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: What moves in Dot
editorial.body: The brief ties every transition to a value (100ms transitions and hover and press states). That is what keeps the page from feeling like a template with an animation preset dropped on top of it. Nothing animates for its own sake in this hero section.

faq.question: Is the Dot prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 800x588, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Do I need React and Tailwind CSS to rebuild Dot?
faq.answer: Dot was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I ship a page rebuilt from Dot without crediting it?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 800x588.

audience: If three people have to edit this hero section, give content leads type from 14px to 72px and 14px spacing steps rather than a screenshot.
People who brief a model on a hero section will use the 3,871-character prompt as the starting point.
